learning_objective: The learner will identify the six parts of a complete reference from a description of each part's look, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** citation-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the six parts of a complete reference from a description of each part's look, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Source Citation, Fact Checking (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A link alone is a complete citation. (2) The year is the date the reader accessed the page. (3) The publisher is the same as the author. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a reference is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of one entry shows how the parts sit together. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part from its place and look. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of one entry in a reference list on a printed page. The entry is made of separate bars on two lines: a short bar for a name, a small bar inside parentheses, a long bar that is drawn as slanted italic text, a medium bar, an underlined bar that looks like a link, and a small bar with a calendar icon beside it. The six markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Author | The short bar at the start of the entry. | The person or organization that created the work, and the first thing a reviewer checks for expertise. | An entry with no author needs extra checking, because no one is accountable for the claim. | | 2 | Year | The small bar inside parentheses after the author. | The year the work was published, which a reviewer compares with the claim's age. | Compare the year with how fast the topic changes. | | 3 | Title | The long slanted bar in the middle of the first line. | The name of the work, which lets a reader search for it. | A title that does not match the claim is a warning sign. | | 4 | Publisher or journal | The medium bar after the title. | The organization or periodical that published the work, which says something about review and reliability. | A reference work from a government agency or a university press has usually been reviewed. | | 5 | Link or identifier | The underlined bar on the second line. | A web address or a persistent identifier, so a reader can open the source. | Test the link, and note the date you tested it. | | 6 | Date accessed | The small bar with a calendar icon at the end. | The date the citing author last saw the page, which matters because web pages change. | A page accessed years ago needs a fresh check. | **Provenance:** The six parts follow the chapter section "Source Citation". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the entry "illustrative example". The sim states that citation styles order the parts differently. **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 6 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 6 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can read a reference." Below 5 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with six numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a complete reference carries the author, the year, the title, the publisher or journal, a link or identifier, and for web pages the date accessed.
